title: What If Earth Sat at the Center of the Galaxy?

scenes.text: What if Earth sat at the center of our galaxy? The night sky would look nothing like ours.
Our nearest star is about four light-years away. At the center, stars sit only 0.4 to 0.04 light-years apart.
NASA says the sky there would be up to one million times denser with stars than the one we know.
Hubble counted more than half a million stars in that core, and about ten million more are too faint to see.
At the very middle sits Sagittarius A star, a black hole about four million times the mass of our Sun.
That crowd equals a million stars packed between us and Alpha Centauri. Our home, 27,000 light-years out, is far quieter.

description:
What if Earth sat at the center of our galaxy?
NASA says stars there are packed up to a million times denser than in our sky, around a black hole of four million Suns.
